subject: an idea for some warning messages

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: an idea for some warning messages
parts:
There are some distributions that we (that is, I) just about never like in a Stan model:
- hard constraints that do not correspond to actual boundaries of parameter space
- inverse-gamma priors with low degrees of freedom
- parameters with super-wide priors such as normal(0,1000)
- uniform distributions
We can probably think of a few more.

Anyway, I’m wondering if the parser should include an option (which by default would be on) to spit out warnings when some of these things are detected.
I can come up with a specific proposal if there is interest. Some natural flags would be upper and lower bounds that are not 0 or 1, inverse-gamma with parameters set to fixed values less than 1, normals with fixed sd’s higher than 100, any uniform distributions, parameters with names that begin with “sigma” that do not have <lower=0>, etc.
Again, just warnings, not errors, and there should be a way to turn the warnings off if it irritates people, but I think this could make a big difference!

A
